objectives.text: Tell binary prefixes (kibi, mebi, gibi, tebi) apart from decimal ones (kilo, mega, giga, tera).
Convert integers between binary, denary, hex and BCD, and use one's and two's complement for negatives.
Add and subtract binary numbers and spot when overflow happens.
Give real uses of BCD and hexadecimal.
Store characters as binary under ASCII, extended ASCII or Unicode.
Explain how bitmaps and vector graphics are encoded, and pick the better one for a job.
Work out bitmap file sizes and how resolution and colour depth change quality and size.
Explain how sound is sampled and how sampling rate and resolution affect size and accuracy.
Compare lossy and lossless compression and say how text, images and sound can be compressed, including RLE.
Describe LANs and WANs, the hardware that builds a LAN, and what a router does.
Compare client-server with peer-to-peer, and thin with thick clients, for a given scenario.
Explain bus, star, mesh and hybrid topologies and how packets move through them.
Describe cloud computing, with its public/private forms, pros and cons.
Compare wired and wireless media (copper, fibre, radio, microwave, satellite).
Explain how Ethernet copes with collisions using CSMA/CD.
Explain real-time and on-demand bit streaming and why bit rate matters.
Separate the web from the internet and describe the hardware that supports the internet.
Explain IPv4/IPv6, subnetting, public vs private and static vs dynamic addresses.
Explain how URLs and DNS find resources on the web.
Explain why computers need input, output, primary and secondary storage, and what buffers do.
Describe embedded systems and weigh their advantages and drawbacks.
Describe how common devices work (printers, microphone, speakers, disks, flash, optical drives, touchscreen, VR headset).
Compare RAM with ROM, SRAM with DRAM, and PROM, EPROM and EEPROM.
Explain monitoring versus control systems, sensors, actuators and feedback.
Know the symbols and truth tables of NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR and XOR.
Build logic circuits from problem statements, expressions or truth tables.
Derive truth tables and logic expressions from circuits, statements or each other.
Explain the Von Neumann model, stored programs, and the roles of registers, ALU, CU, clock and IAS.
Describe how the address, data and control buses move data, and how ports link peripherals.
Explain how cores, bus width, clock speed and cache affect performance.
Describe the fetch-execute cycle in register transfer notation.
Explain what interrupts are and how the processor detects and services them.
Relate assembly language to machine code and describe a two-pass assembler.
Trace and write simple assembly programs using the instruction groups and addressing modes.
Apply shifts and bit masks to test, set and control bits.
Explain why an OS is needed and what it manages (memory, files, security, hardware, processes).
Describe the utility programs that ship with an OS.
Explain program libraries and the benefit of DLLs.
Explain when assemblers, compilers and interpreters are needed and weigh compiler against interpreter.
Describe IDE features for coding, error detection, presentation and debugging.
Distinguish security, privacy and integrity of data.
Describe measures protecting systems from a single PC to a network.
Describe threats from networks (malware, hacking, phishing, pharming) and ways to reduce them.
Explain how validation and verification protect integrity.
Apply validation checks (range, format, length, presence, existence, limit, check digit).
Apply verification during entry (visual, double entry) and transfer (parity, checksum).
Explain why computing professionals need ethics and bodies like BCS and IEEE.
Judge the effects of ethical and unethical behaviour in a scenario.
Explain why copyright law is needed.
Compare software licences (free, open source, shareware, commercial) and justify a choice.
Describe AI applications and their social, economic and environmental impact.
Explain the weaknesses of file-based storage and how relational databases fix them.
Use relational terminology (keys, tuples, relationships, referential integrity, indexing) and draw E-R diagrams.
Normalise data to 1NF, 2NF and 3NF and justify whether tables meet 3NF.
Describe what a DBMS provides (data dictionary, modelling, schema, integrity, security) and its developer interface and query processor.
Explain that DDL changes structure and DML handles queries and maintenance, both through SQL.
Write SQL DDL to create databases and tables, alter them and set primary and foreign keys.
Write SQL DML to query and change data across up to two tables.
Explain abstraction and build abstract models of systems.
Break problems down using decomposition into modules.
Define an algorithm and represent its data with identifier tables.
Write pseudocode using sequence, selection and iteration with input, process and output.
Convert between structured English, flowcharts and pseudocode.
Refine an algorithm step by step and use logic statements to define parts of it.
Choose suitable data types for a problem and define records in pseudocode.
Use 1D and 2D arrays, including bounds, and process them with bubble sort and linear search.
Explain why files are needed and read and write text files in pseudocode.
Explain ADTs and the features and uses of stacks, queues and linked lists.
Add, edit and delete data in stacks, queues and linked lists.
Describe how stacks, queues and linked lists can be built using arrays.
Turn flowcharts or structured English into pseudocode with constants, variables, assignment and I/O.
Use built-in functions and library routines.
Write IF, CASE and the three loop types, and justify the choice of loop.
Define and use procedures and functions, and decide when each is appropriate.
Use parameters passed by value or reference and the associated terminology.
Write efficient pseudocode.
Describe the development life cycle stages and compare waterfall, iterative and RAD.
Design with structure charts and state-transition diagrams.
Identify and correct syntax, logic and run-time errors.
Select testing methods and test data (normal, abnormal, boundary) and explain test plans.
Distinguish perfective, adaptive and corrective maintenance.
Analyse and amend an existing program to add functionality.
Explain why user-defined types are needed and define non-composite (enumerated, pointer) and composite (set, record, class) types.
Choose serial, sequential or random file organisation and the matching access method.
Use hashing algorithms to store and find records in files.
Describe floating-point format and how mantissa and exponent sizes affect range and precision.
Convert floating-point and denary values both ways and normalise.
Explain approximation, rounding errors, overflow and underflow in binary representation.
Explain why protocols and layered stacks are essential.
Describe the four TCP/IP layers and how a message travels between hosts.
State the purposes of HTTP, FTP, POP3, IMAP, SMTP and BitTorrent.
Compare circuit switching and packet switching, including the router's role.
Compare RISC and CISC, including pipelining and interrupt handling.
Describe SISD, SIMD, MISD and MIMD and massively parallel computers.
Explain virtual machines with their benefits and limits.
Produce truth tables for circuits including half and full adders.
Explain SR and JK flip-flops as storage elements.
Simplify logic using Boolean algebra, De Morgan's laws and Karnaugh maps.
Explain how an OS maximises resource use and hides hardware complexity.
Describe process states and scheduling routines, and how the kernel handles interrupts.
Explain virtual memory, paging, segmentation, page replacement and thrashing.
Describe how interpreters run code and the stages of compilation.
Express grammar with syntax diagrams or BNF.
Evaluate expressions with Reverse Polish Notation.
Explain symmetric and asymmetric encryption and how keys give privacy and verification.
Explain quantum cryptography's purpose, benefits and drawbacks.
Describe SSL/TLS and when to use it.
Explain how digital certificates are obtained and used for digital signatures.
Explain how graphs support AI and trace A* and Dijkstra's searches.
Explain how neural networks help machine learning.
Compare deep, machine (supervised/unsupervised) and reinforcement learning.
Explain back propagation and regression in machine learning.
Write and compare linear and binary search, including when binary search applies.
Write insertion and bubble sort and explain what affects their performance.
Write algorithms to find, insert and delete items in stacks, queues, linked lists and binary trees.
Describe graphs as ADTs and build ADTs (including dictionaries) from other types.
Compare algorithms using time and space, including Big O notation.
Write and trace recursive algorithms, judge when recursion helps, and explain how compilers handle it with stacks.
Explain what a programming paradigm is.
Write low-level and imperative code using the various addressing modes and procedures.
Use OOP terminology and design and write classes using inheritance, polymorphism and encapsulation.
Write declarative facts and rules to satisfy a goal.
Perform file operations (open, close, read and write records) on serial, sequential and random files.
Explain and write exception handling.
